A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Solving Inverse Problems with FLAIR. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction experiments on FFHQ and DIV2K, component ablations, posterior-variance measurements, image editing, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds pixel-space comparisons, runtime and memory measurements, ensemble experiments, and repeated-reconstruction statistical evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the flow-matching objective, deterministic trajectory adjustment, calibrated weighting, and alternating regularization/data-consistency updates. Initialization notation is generalized. The pixel-space, smaller-VAE, step-budget, and ensemble experiments extend configurations and analyses without establishing a new core solver component.

E1.justification: V2 adds CelebA-HQ through a pretrained pixel-space flow model and evaluation on 1,000 images for inpainting and ×8 super-resolution (Section 5.2, Appendix A.9). This extends dataset coverage within the existing face-restoration domain; the FFHQ/DIV2K tasks and editing examples remain.

E2.justification: The original ReSample, FlowDPS, RSD, and FlowChef comparisons remain. V2 adds an evaluated pixel-space comparison suite containing DDNM, DPS, Moment Matching, and ΠGDM (main Table 2, Appendix Table 5). Their earlier citation or use as implementation references did not constitute these comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 adds evaluation with a 256×256 pixel-space backbone, runtime comparisons using different VAEs/data-step budgets, eight-prediction ensembles, and smaller-subset statistical experiments. Appendix A.5 changes FlowChef inpainting from 50 to 200 NFE despite the retained equal-budget statement. Main Table 1 changes the noise label from 0.01 to 0.5%, while appendix tables retain 0.01; these reporting revisions do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.10 tests the speed, memory, and reconstruction-quality effects of a tiny VAE and at most five data-term steps. A.11 compares individual predictions with eight-sample averages to investigate posterior-mean estimation and perceptual tradeoffs. Existing component, weighting, captioning, posterior-variance, and failure-case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V1 already reports sample-wise standard deviations and 32-sample posterior variability. V2 additionally reports three reconstructions per input on 100 FFHQ and 80 DIV2K images, standard deviations of aggregate metrics including FID, matched random seeds, and paired LPIPS t-tests against FlowDPS (Appendix A.12, Tables 8–16). This adds distinct uncertainty and significance assessments.

E6.justification: V2 adds pixel-space, runtime, ensemble, and repeated-reconstruction results. It also revises baseline FID entries: for DIV2K ×8 super-resolution, FlowDPS changes from 54.2 to 44.4 and FlowChef from 48.6 to 36.5. FLAIR's main Table 1 values and original component-ablation values remain unchanged. The new experiments have separate settings and do not establish improvements over v1's FLAIR scores.

T1.justification: The propositions and Appendix A.1–A.3 derivations are substantially retained. V2 makes time averaging explicit in gradient expressions and adds weighted-gradient Equation 10. As printed, that equation weights only the learned velocity, whereas Algorithm 1 weights the entire velocity difference, introducing a localized mathematical inconsistency.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion replace the claim that trajectory adjustment recovers rare or atypical modes with guidance toward posterior-likely, observation-consistent images. This qualifies one advertised contribution while retaining the framework's novelty, hard-consistency, calibration, reconstruction-quality, and diversity claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets ensemble PSNR gains as evidence that samples surround the posterior mean and discusses broader pixel-space applicability and speed-quality tradeoffs. Existing limitations and failure explanations remain. The new ensemble interpretation overstates Table 7: FLAIR's LPIPS increases with averaging despite prose saying it decreases, and its PSNR gain is not consistently the largest.

D1.justification: V2 adds a stated source-code access link in the abstract, tuned likelihood weights and a regularizer scale for pixel-space experiments, runtime/memory measurements, and explicit pFID patch counts. The existing detailed SD3 implementation, hardware, preprocessing, and default optimization disclosures are largely retained. The linked resource itself was not inspected.

R1.justification: Seven cited works are added, covering mixture guidance, divide-and-conquer sampling, midpoint guidance, decoupled noise annealing, the Moment Matching reference, and multimodal image fusion. These extend citations and support the new comparison, while Section 2's central positioning relative to variational posterior sampling remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 locally rewrites the abstract and contribution statements, clarifies initialization and terminology, corrects some notation and language, adds acknowledgments, and inserts new appendix subsections. The main section order and most existing explanatory prose remain intact; this is not an extensive narrative reorganization.

P2.justification: V2 adds a pixel-space comparison table and figure, displayed in both the main text and appendix, plus runtime, ensemble, repeated-reconstruction, and significance tables. Existing main-text displays are repositioned and some labels reformatted; appendix numbering restarts. The original qualitative and failure galleries are retained. These additions substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves empirical assessability: the additional pixel-space prior and four comparators test applicability beyond the original latent implementation, repeated reconstructions address stochastic reliability, and runtime/memory analysis exposes previously unreported practical costs. These resolve important validation gaps in v1. The gains are tempered by conflicting noise/NFE descriptions, the new gradient-expression inconsistency, and ensemble claims that contradict Table 7, but the added evidence still provides a substantial net improvement.
